text: The shortest war in history lasted about thirty-eight minutes. You've had longer phone calls.
Zanzibar, August eighteen ninety-six. The sultan dies, and his cousin Khalid moves into the palace without asking Britain first.
Britain disagrees. It parks warships in the harbour, and sends a note: leave by nine o'clock tomorrow morning.
Khalid barricades the palace, and waits.
Nine o'clock arrives. The ships open fire.
The palace catches fire. And the sultan's entire navy, one royal yacht, sinks in the harbour.
Khalid? He slips out the back, and hides in the German consulate.
By about nine forty, the guns stop. A new sultan is in charge before lunch.
Short, but not painless. Hundreds were hurt in the palace.
Luckily, it was over before breakfast went cold. Unluckily, the losing side was sent the bill for the shells.
Thirty-eight minutes. Still the shortest war ever recorded.
